source_text: Περὶ τοῦ τοὺς ἐπισκόπους κρίσει τῶν μητροπολιτῶν καὶ τῶν πέριξ ἐπισκόπων καθίστασθαι εἰς τὴν ἐκκλησιαστικὴν ἀρχήν, ὄντας ἐκ πολλοῦ δεδοκιμασμένους ἔν τε τῷ λόγῳ τῆς πίστεως, καὶ τῇ τοῦ εὐθέος βίου πολιτείᾳ. Ἐ ρ μ η ν ε ί α. Ὁ παρών Κανών διορίζει, ὅτι μὲ τὴν κρίσιν καὶ ψῆφον τῶν πέριξ Μητροπολιτῶν καὶ Ἐπισκόπων τῆς ἐπαρχίας νά γίνωνται οἱ χειροτονούμενοι Ἐπίσκοποι, ὄντες πρὸ πολλῶν χρόνων δεδοκιμασμένοι καὶ μαρτυρημένοι, καὶ κατὰ τὰ ὀρθόδοξα δόγματα τῆς πίστεως, καὶ κατὰ τὴν μὲ ὀρθὸν λόγον γινομένην ἐνάρετον πολιτείαν. Ὅρᾳ καὶ τὸν α΄. Ἀποστολικόν, καὶ τὸν δ΄. τῆς α΄.
thought_title: Bishops appointed by metropolitan judgment after long testing
orientation: The council is decreeing how bishops are to be appointed to ecclesiastical office, requiring the judgment of the metropolitan and neighboring bishops and prior testing in faith and upright life.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the bishops being appointed to the ecclesiastical office by the judgment of the metropolitans and of the surrounding bishops, being long since tested both in the word of the faith and in the conduct of upright life. Interpretation. The present Canon ordains that the bishops being ordained should be made with the judgment and vote of the surrounding Metropolitans and Bishops of the province, being for many years before tested and witnessed, both according to the orthodox doctrines of the faith, and according to the virtuous conduct that comes about with right reason. See also the 1st Apostolic, and the 4th of the 1st.

choices.english: by the judgment of the metropolitans
choices.why: The source uses κρίσις for the formal decision of the metropolitan, distinct from the vote (ψῆφος) of the surrounding bishops; rendering both as 'judgment' and 'vote' preserves the two-step process.
rejected: by the decision of the metropolitans
by the approval of the metropolitans

choices.english: to be appointed to the ecclesiastical office
choices.why: ἀρχή here means the ruling office of bishop, not a generic 'rule'; 'ecclesiastical office' captures the institutional sense.
rejected: to be established in the church's rule
to be set over the church

choices.english: in the conduct of upright life
choices.why: πολιτεία means manner of life or conduct; εὐθέος βίου is 'of upright life'; the phrase describes the tested moral character, not civic life.
rejected: in the citizenship of a straight life
in the uprightness of life's conduct

choices.why: ἐκ πολλοῦ means 'from long ago' or 'for a long time'; the perfect participle δεδοκιμασμένους indicates a completed testing that stands as qualification.

choices.term: κατὰ τὴν μὲ ὀρθὸν λόγον γινομένην ἐνάρετον πολιτείαν
choices.english: according to the virtuous conduct that comes about with right reason
choices.why: The interpretation expands the canon's 'upright life' with ὀρθὸν λόγον ('right reason') as the source of virtuous conduct; the gloss keeps the causal force of γινομένην.
rejected: according to the virtuous citizenship made by right word
according to the virtuous conduct made with right speech

pass_b_english: Concerning the appointment of bishops to the ecclesiastical office by the judgment of the metropolitans and the surrounding bishops, they being long since tested both in the word of faith and in the conduct of upright life.

Interpretation. The present canon decrees that those being ordained bishops are to be made so by the judgment and vote of the surrounding metropolitans and bishops of the province, they having been tested and witnessed for many years beforehand, both according to the orthodox doctrines of the faith and according to the virtuous conduct that comes about with right reason. See also Apostolic Canon 1 and Canon 4 of the First Council.

last_rejected.why: Source says surrounding metropolitans AND bishops, but English reverses to metropolitans and surrounding bishops, changing which group is modified.
last_rejected.fix: the surrounding metropolitans and bishops of the province
last_rejected.ruling: πέριξ modifies both Μητροπολιτῶν and Ἐπισκόπων; English 'surrounding metropolitans and bishops' preserves this correctly.

last_rejected.quote: both according to the orthodox doctrines
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ κατὰ τὰ ὀρθόδοξα δόγματα τῆς πίστεως, καὶ κατὰ τὴν μὲ ὀρθὸν λόγον γινομένην ἐνάρετον πολιτείαν
last_rejected.why: Source has two κατά phrases ('both according to... and according to'); English drops first καί, weakening the dual requirement.
last_rejected.fix: both according to the orthodox doctrines of the faith, and according to the virtuous conduct that comes about with right reason
last_rejected.ruling: English 'both according to...and according to' renders καὶ...καὶ correctly; no καί is dropped.
